questions.question_text: An LSAC Law School Forum is scheduled for Saturday in Washington, D.C. A candidate needs to attend a workshop one hour prior to the forum. If the forum begins at 10:00 a.m., at what time must the candidate attend the workshop?
questions.explanation: If the forum starts at 10:00 a.m. and the workshop is one hour prior, then 10:00 minus 1 hour equals 9:00 a.m.

questions.question_text: LSAC sets specific eligibility requirements for the 'Plus, Guided Journey' program. An applicant must be a U.S. citizen OR a permanent resident alien OR have DACA status. Which of the following applicants is ineligible?
options: An applicant who is a U.S. citizen.
An applicant who is a permanent resident alien with an I-551 card.
An applicant who has been granted DACA status.
An applicant who is a foreign national with no legal residency or status in the U.S.
questions.explanation: The program requires specific legal statuses (Citizen, Permanent Resident, or DACA). An applicant with no such status does not meet the criteria provided.

questions.question_text: A student is planning to attend a series of workshops. There are four workshops available: Ethics, Admissions, Financing, and Diversity. The student must attend exactly three of them. If the student attends Financing, they cannot attend Diversity. Which of the following could be the student's schedule?
questions.explanation: The student must choose 3 workshops. Since they cannot attend both Financing and Diversity, they must drop one of those. Ethics and Admissions must be included to reach the count of 3.

questions.question_text: Four students (A, B, C, D) are meeting with law school representatives. Only one student can speak at a time. A must speak before B. C must speak after D. D must speak first. What is the correct order of speakers?
questions.explanation: D is first. C must be after D. A must be before B. Placing D first and then A, B, and C satisfies all conditions.

questions.question_text: An LSAC Forum host needs to schedule three events (Workshop, Q&A, and Networking) between 5 p.m. and 8 p.m. Each event is 1 hour long. The Q&A must come immediately after the Workshop. If the Workshop starts at 5 p.m., when does Networking start?
questions.explanation: Workshop (5-6), Q&A (6-7), Networking (7-8). Networking starts at 7 p.m.

questions.question_text: Three candidates are applying for a scholarship. Candidate X has a higher LSAT score than Y. Candidate Z has a lower score than X but a higher score than Y. Who has the lowest score?
questions.explanation: X > Y and X > Z > Y. Therefore, Y is at the bottom of the list.

questions.question_text: Four students (A, B, C, D) are meeting with representatives, one at a time. A must speak before B. C must speak after D. D must speak first. What is the correct order?
questions.explanation: D is first. A must be before B, and C must be after D. In D, A, B, C, all conditions are satisfied.

questions.question_text: An LSAC host schedules three 1-hour events (Workshop, Q&A, Networking) between 5 p.m. and 8 p.m. Q&A must follow the Workshop immediately. If the Workshop starts at 5 p.m., when does Networking start?
Five law school representatives (P, Q, R, S, T) are assigned to booths 1 through 5. P is not in booth 1. Q is in booth 2. R is in an even-numbered booth. If T is in booth 5, which booth is S in?
questions.explanation: Q is in 2, T is in 5. R must be in 4 (the only even number left). P cannot be in 1, so P must be in 3. S must be in 1.

questions.question_text: A schedule includes three seminars: Environmental Law, Tax Law, and Family Law. If Environmental Law must be either first or last, and Tax Law is not immediately after Environmental Law, which order is valid?
questions.explanation: In Env, Fam, Tax, Env is first and Tax is not immediately after it, satisfying all rules.

questions.question_text: A committee of 3 must be chosen from A, B, C, D, and E. If A must be included, and B cannot be with C, which group is possible?
questions.explanation: Must have A. If we have C, we cannot have B. A, C, D fits.
